key_insight: KATOsuper makes topology optimization faster and more stable by using a sensitivity-consistent Fourier neural operator so the predicted objective and its gradient stay aligned during optimization.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical surrogate-accelerated compliance and stress design for 2D and 3D structures, with large deployment-time speedups while preserving competitive topology quality.
method: Forward_split SC-FNO computes sensitivities by automatic differentiation through the predicted objective field.
Physics-informed multi-channel inputs plus Fourier position embeddings support resolution-invariant learning and zero-shot extrapolation.
KATO3D extends the framework to 3D with KANConv3D blocks and learnable B-spline activations.
evidence_signal: Across three 2D benchmarks and three 3D cases, the method reports about 15–110x deployment-time speedup over MATLAB baselines, with stronger gains in complex 3D and stress-optimization problems.
watch_item: Zero-shot scaling can preserve topology at high resolution factors, but practical accuracy depends on consistent sensitivity direction, so approximation error in the physics surrogate still needs careful validation.
paper_title: KATOsuper: Surrogate-accelerated neural topology optimization with sensitivity-consistent Fourier neural operators
